key_idea: Minimum flights = (minimum vertex-disjoint path cover of the DAG) - 1 = n - maxmatching - 1, and a city's airport is reachable iff it can be a path endpoint in some minimum cover, i.e. its out-copy or in-copy is unmatched in some maximum matching.
sketch: Build the bipartite graph out(u) - in(v) per train edge and run Hopcroft-Karp. Paths can be ordered arbitrarily, so any vertex that is a path end can be placed non-last and any path start non-first; hence with at least 2 paths the airport set is exactly the vertices that are a start or end in some min cover. A left vertex can be left unmatched in some maximum matching iff it is reachable from a free left vertex by an alternating path (unmatched edge to the right, matched edge back); do one BFS from free left vertices and a symmetric one from free right vertices on the reversed graph. Output the union sorted. O(m sqrt n). Pitfalls: when the cover is a single path the answer is 0 and a blank line, even though the path has endpoints. Stress-tested against permutation brute force for n <= 7.
